trap-thesis-restatement.notes: SEPARATE (non-trap) findings. (1) The k = 1 contradiction recorded on prop:jucys-murphy-central-elements-qou originates HERE, in Step 3 (J_k v_T = q^(2c) v_T against the proposition's J_1 = empty sum = 0), and Step 2 confirms the additive reading by expanding P_1 = J_1 + ... + J_n = sum_{i<k} q^(1-k) sigma_{i,k}. (2) PROOF GAP in Step 2: 'P_1 ... is centralised by every sigma_j (each sigma_j acts on the sum by permuting the transpositions, fixing the symmetric sum)'. That is the C[S_n] class-sum argument, where sum over ALL transpositions is central because it is a conjugacy class. Here the summands carry q^(1-k) weights that are NOT permutation-symmetric in k, so the sum is not a class sum and the permutation argument does not transfer at q != 1. 'their sigma_j-invariance follows from the same permutation argument applied at the level of multi-index summations' inherits the same gap. The result (Murphy 1992) is true; the argument given for it is not. (3) LIKELY DOUBLE NORMALISATION in the Corollary: T^(l) = m_e . (sum_{lambda |- 3A, ht = l+1} w_lambda(q) c_l(lambda)) / [3A]_q!, with w_lambda(q) defined two lines below as dim_q(lambda)^2 / [n]_q! and n = 3A here - so [3A]_q! divides twice, giving ([3A]_q!)^2 in the denominator. The same doubling carries into the alpha_5 formula.
